articles.simple: As Chinese President Xi Jinping prepares for a Washington visit, China has slapped new restrictions involving drones as part of its own retaliatory trade measures against the US.
articles.background: US-China trade tensions have featured escalating tit-for-tat export controls on strategically sensitive technology (chips, rare earths, and now drones), continuing even as high-level diplomatic visits are being planned.
articles.relevance: Shows continued friction in the US-China relationship even amid diplomatic engagement efforts.

articles.headline: Back on AIway, Nasdaq Mcap Swells by $3.5 Tn in 4 Days
articles.original: The Nasdaq's total market capitalisation grew by $3.5 trillion over four days, driven by renewed AI-stock enthusiasm.

terms.d: Market capitalisation — the total value of a company's (or in this case, an index's) outstanding shares.

articles.simple: US tech stocks on the Nasdaq added a combined $3.5 trillion in value over just four trading days, powered by renewed excitement around AI.
articles.background: This rally likely reflects a mix of factors also reported elsewhere in this edition — easing oil prices reducing inflation worries, hopes the Fed has room to stay accommodative, and continued heavy AI infrastructure investment (including the Anthropic-Volta and Nvidia-related deals reported this week).
articles.relevance: A striking reflection of just how much of current US stock market gains are being driven by AI-related enthusiasm.

articles.headline: Monsoon Watch
articles.original: Isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall very likely over East & Northeast India during next 5-6 days.
articles.simple: Heavy rain is forecast for East and Northeast India over the next several days, per the daily weather round-up.
articles.background: 'Monsoon Watch' is a regular daily weather-forecast feature in this edition rather than a standalone news story.
articles.relevance: Relevant to agriculture, flood preparedness and daily life across East and Northeast India this week.

articles.headline: Regulators Eye CRILC Cover for Surety Bonds
articles.original: Regulators are considering bringing surety bonds under CRILC reporting coverage.

terms.d: Central Repository of Information on Large Credits — an RBI database that tracks large borrower credit exposures across banks to help spot early signs of stress.
A three-party guarantee where an insurer promises to cover a loss if a contractor/borrower fails to meet its obligations, often used as an alternative to bank guarantees.

articles.simple: Regulators want surety bond exposures tracked in the same large-credit database banks already use, to better monitor risk in this fast-growing product.
articles.background: Surety bonds have been actively promoted by Indian regulators (particularly for infrastructure projects) as a bank-guarantee alternative, and as the market grows, extending standard credit-monitoring tools to it is a natural next regulatory step.
articles.relevance: Relevant to insurers and infrastructure companies increasingly relying on surety bonds instead of traditional bank guarantees.

articles.headline: Niti Calls for Policy to Aid, Regulate Caregiving MSMEs
articles.original: Government think tank Niti Aayog has called for a policy framework to support and regulate small businesses (MSMEs) in the caregiving sector.

terms.d: India's central government policy think tank.
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

articles.simple: Niti Aayog wants the government to create rules and support systems for small businesses that provide elder-care, childcare and similar caregiving services.
articles.background: India's rapidly ageing population and rising dual-income households have fuelled demand for organised caregiving services, an informal sector that currently lacks much regulatory structure or dedicated policy support.
articles.relevance: Could shape future support and standards for India's growing but currently informal caregiving industry.

articles.headline: Services PMI Hits 53-month Low in July
articles.original: India's Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to a 53-month low in July.

terms.d: Purchasing Managers' Index — a survey-based indicator of business activity; above 50 signals expansion, below 50 signals contraction.

articles.simple: Growth in India's services sector slowed to its weakest pace in more than four years last month.
articles.background: The services PMI is a closely watched monthly gauge of business sentiment and activity; a multi-year low would raise questions about near-term momentum in India's dominant services economy, even as the RBI (elsewhere in this edition) sounded relatively upbeat on overall growth.
articles.relevance: An important, somewhat cautionary economic data point worth watching alongside the RBI's more optimistic growth outlook.

articles.headline: ISI Bill Proposes New Governance Framework
articles.original: A bill related to the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) proposes a new governance framework for the institution.

terms.d: In this context, likely the Indian Statistical Institute, a premier national institution for statistics, mathematics and data science.

articles.simple: New legislation aims to overhaul how one of India's premier statistics and data-science institutions is governed.
articles.background: Reforming governance structures at premier national academic/research institutions has been a recurring policy theme as India seeks to modernise higher-education administration.
articles.relevance: Relevant to the governance and academic administration of a key Indian scientific/statistical institution.

articles.headline: Inventory Only Against Export Orders for Ecomm
articles.original: A new rule reportedly requires e-commerce companies to hold inventory only against confirmed export orders.

terms.d: E-commerce.

articles.simple: E-commerce companies may now need to keep stock only for goods they already have confirmed export orders for, rather than stockpiling speculatively.
articles.background: This type of rule is typically aimed at customs/trade facilitation or bonded-warehouse schemes for export-oriented e-commerce, helping tighten compliance and reduce speculative stockpiling under duty-benefit schemes.
articles.relevance: Relevant to e-commerce exporters and how they manage inventory and customs compliance.

articles.headline: Parliament Watch
articles.original: A recurring round-up feature tracking bills and business before India's Parliament; several related items (the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, the Supreme Court judges' strength bill, the parliamentary deadlock) are covered elsewhere in this edition.
articles.simple: A regular column tracking what's happening in Parliament this session — not a standalone story on its own.
articles.background: 'Parliament Watch' is a recurring feature consolidating parliamentary business rather than one specific news item.
articles.relevance: See the related Pure Politics section entries for the specific bills and issues before Parliament this session.

articles.headline: SECI Seeks CO₂ Suppliers for Green Urea, Methanol Projects
articles.original: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) is seeking suppliers of captured CO₂ for green urea and methanol projects.

terms.d: Solar Energy Corporation of India, a state-run renewable energy implementing agency.
Urea or methanol produced using low-carbon or renewable inputs (like green hydrogen and captured CO₂) instead of conventional fossil-fuel-based processes.

articles.simple: SECI is inviting companies that can supply captured carbon dioxide to support new green fertiliser and green methanol projects.
articles.background: India has been promoting green hydrogen and related green-chemical value chains (including green ammonia/urea) as part of its energy transition and fertiliser-import-reduction strategy, and captured CO₂ is a key input for methanol production.
articles.relevance: Relevant to India's green hydrogen ecosystem and efforts to reduce reliance on imported fertiliser.

articles.headline: Customs Readies Playbook for 100Key Imports to Reap FTA Benefits
articles.original: India's customs authorities are preparing a playbook covering 100 key import categories to help businesses better claim benefits under free trade agreements (FTAs).

terms.d: Free Trade Agreement — a pact between countries that reduces tariffs and trade barriers between them.

articles.simple: Customs officials are creating detailed guidance for around 100 major import categories to help Indian importers properly claim the lower tariffs available under trade agreements.
articles.background: Businesses often under-utilise FTA tariff benefits due to complex rules-of-origin compliance requirements; clearer customs guidance could help more importers actually capture the savings these agreements are meant to offer.
articles.relevance: Could help Indian businesses better realise cost savings from India's growing network of trade agreements.

articles.headline: ONGC Targets Oil Blocks in Venezuela
articles.original: State-run ONGC is targeting new oil block acquisitions in Venezuela.

terms.d: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, India's largest state-run oil and gas exploration company.

articles.simple: India's top state oil explorer, ONGC, is looking to acquire oil exploration blocks in Venezuela.
articles.background: ONGC Videsh (ONGC's overseas arm) has historically held stakes in Venezuelan oil assets as part of India's strategy to diversify crude oil sourcing and reduce reliance on West Asian supply, a strategy that gains added relevance given the West Asia tensions referenced elsewhere in this edition.
articles.relevance: Relevant to India's energy security strategy and diversification of crude oil supply sources.
